  "content": "---\nid: pi0-grasp-tall-mug-by-handle\nscope: global\nkind: primitive\ntitle: Grasp a tall wide-mouth mug by its handle, not from above\napplies_when: picking a tall mug/cup whose open top is wider than the gripper, where\n  pi0_pick keeps descending into the cup and grabbing air\nsymptom:\n- pi0 descends into mug\n- gripper stays open ~0.06\n- peak_lift ~0\n- grabbed air\n- mug not lifted\n- cup interior visible in wrist\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t6_s0\n  attempts: 3\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- pi0-pick-prompt-specificity\n---\n\n\nFor a tall mug with a mouth wider than the gripper opening, `pi0_pick \"grasp the\n{color} mug\"` drives the gripper straight down into the open top and closes on\nnothing; prompt it to grasp the HANDLE instead.\n\n**Why:** The default pick prompt makes pi0 aim at the object's top-center. On a\nwide-mouth mug the two fingers straddle the rim and enter the cavity, so closing\ngrips air (finger separation stays ~0.06, no lift). The thin side handle is a\nsolid, narrow feature pi0 can pinch (finger separation closes to ~0.01).\n**How to apply:** Pre-position ~15-20 cm above the mug, offset the eef slightly\ntoward the handle side / +y, then `pi0_pick \"grasp the {color} mug by the handle\"`\nwith max_chunks 12-18. Confirm grip_opening ~0.01 and peak_lift > 0.15. pi0 often\nalso auto-carries the eef forward after lifting \u2014 that is fine; firm with\nset_gripper +1 and take over the carry. The mug then hangs with its base offset\n~(+0.05,-0.03 m) from the eef; place by putting eef = target - that offset and\ndescending until OSC stalls (base contact).\n**Falsify:** A tall mug that pi0 lifts cleanly from the plain top-center prompt\n(narrow mouth), or a handle-grasp that fails to close on the handle.\n**Related:** [[predicate-gated-by-eef-proximity-retreat-clear]]\n"
}

The real\ndifficulties are NOT the grasps \u2014 they are (a) the tall mug's grasp geometry,\n(b) the ordering so the second carry does not tip the first placement, and\n(c) two predicate subtleties: the \"right\" side sign, and an eef-proximity gate.\n\n## Winning technique\nOrder: PUDDING FIRST, MUG LAST (never carry/re-grasp over the placed mug).\n1. Pre-position ~(mug_x, mug_y+0.045, 0.62); `pi0_pick \"grasp the red mug by the\n   handle\"` (chunks ~15). pi0 hooks the thin handle (grip ~0.01, lift ~0.20) and\n   auto-drives the eef forward to ~plate x. `set_gripper +1`.\n5. Position eef = plate_center - (0.05,-0.03) [the held-mug base hangs ~+0.05 x,\n   -0.03 y from the eef]; descend until OSC stalls (~z0.57 = mug base on plate);\n   `release`.   "content": "---\nid: libero10-left-right-sign-verify-empirically\nscope: global\nkind: perception\ntitle: Do not trust a fixed left/right sign for \"right/left of X\" predicates; verify\n  empirically\napplies_when: a task says put an object to the left/right of a reference and you must\n  choose +y vs -y for the placement\nsymptom:\n- put to the right of the plate\n- left/right of\n- egocentric\n- geometrically clean placement no termination\n- wrong side\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t6_s0\n  attempts: 3\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- predicate-gated-by-eef-proximity-retreat-clear\n---\n\n\nThe \"right\"/\"left of X\" goal predicate sign is NOT reliably robot-egocentric:\nin libero_10 task-t6 \"to the right of the plate\" fired for +y (IMAGE-RIGHT /\nviewer perspective), the OPPOSITE of the common egocentric rule (+y=robot-left=\nimage-right, so right=-y). Verify the side empirically instead of assuming.\n\n**Why:** observed. The corpus egocentric heuristic (+y = robot-left = image-right)\npredicts right = -y = image-left, but this cell's predicate evaluated the pudding\n\"to the right of the plate\" as satisfied at +y and unsatisfied at -y. The sign\nconvention of the underlying spatial predicate here is viewer/world +y = \"right\",\nnot robot-egocentric. Do not over-generalize either sign.\n**How to apply:** When a clean placement of the CORRECT object on your guessed\nside does not terminate (and the eef is retreated clear, see related), flip to\nthe OTHER side before suspecting the co-clause (e.g. the On() half). Budget one\nprobe per new seed: place, retreat clear, check; if false and geometry is clean,\ntry the opposite y-sign. Keep the co-object's placement fixed while flipping.\n**Falsify:** A libero_10 left/right cell that fires on the egocentric side\n(right=-y), confirming the egocentric rule for that task \u2014 record it as a\ncounter-example so the sign is treated as task-specific, not global.\n**Related:** [[predicate-gated-by-eef-proximity-retreat-clear]]\n"
}
